question: In September 2021, ______ became the first Indian woman to win two Paralympic medals.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Avani Lekhara.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **In September 2021, Avani Lekhara became the first Indian woman to win two Paralympic medals.** 
 
• Avani Lekhara, a para shooter, made history by becoming the** first Indian woman** to take home two medals from the Paralympics.
 
• The 19-year-old rifle shooter now has a bronze medal in the **women's 50m rifle 3-position SH1 event after winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle shooting SH1 class in Tokyo.**
 
• She also became the** first Indian woman to win two medals at the Para Games in the same edition**. After qualifying for the final in the second position with 1176 points, Avani Lekhara continued her momentum in the medal round as well.
 
• The Jaipur-based shooter, who suffered spinal cord injuries in a car accident in 2012, had fired a total of 249.6 shots, which was a new Paralympic record and tied the world record.
 
• Prior to her, **Joginder Singh Sodhi** was the lone Indian to win multiple medals in the same edition of the Games when he fetched one silver and two bronze medals in the 1984 Paralympics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Bhavina Patel
 Bhavina Hasmukhbhai Patel is an Indian parathlete and table tennis player from Mehsana, Gujarat. At the Tokyo 2020 Summer Paralympics, she took home a silver medal in Class 4 Table Tennis.
 
 

 Ekta Bhyan
 Ekta Bhyan is a para athlete who represents India in the women's club and discus throw events. She competed on behalf of her country at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, Indonesia, where she won the club throw gold medal.
 
 

 Deepa Malik
 Deepa Malik is an Indian athlete. She started her career at the age of 30. She won a silver medal in the shot put event at the 2016 Summer Paralympics, becoming the first Indian woman to do so. At the 2018 paralympic Grand Prix in Dubai, she also took home gold in the F-53/54 Javelin competition.
